The search results show several *related* historical PRs addressing similar `local.agent.current()` undefined issues (PRs #7689, #7748, #7747, #7796, #7940, #7920), but these are all closed/merged fixes from earlier development. PR #8635 is a new PR addressing fresh crash bugs (#8588, #8579, #8580) with different root causes and solutions, so it is not a duplicate of any currently open PR.

> This means session data was sent to OpenCode's servers without explicit notice, raising potential privacy concerns.

If you don't want opencode provider to be active, you can disable it in your config:
```
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "disabled_providers": ["opencode"]
}
```
Or it's also possible to configure a whitelist-only using `enabled_providers`.

What I agree is done incorrectly in the linked functions is this:
```
    if (providerID.startsWith("github-copilot")) {
        // prioritize free models for github copilot
        priority = ["gpt-5-mini", "claude-haiku-4.5", ...priority]
    }
```
claude-haiku-4.5 has a cost of [0.33 premium requests](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/copilot-requests#model-multipliers) per request, it's absolutely not free; if more models are needed than just gpt-5-mini, then gpt-4.1 is another candidate

More importantly, the actual default behavior—silently sending data to a third-party service (opencode) when the user has configured a different primary provider—constitutes a privacy issue and should be clearly communicated.

I had the same problem using the desktop version where unshare is not implemented - I was able to manually delete the share like this:
1) locate the session-share {id} and {secret}. On windows this was located in `../users/{user}/.local/share/opencode/storage/session_share/`,
2) run `curl -X DELETE "https://opncd.ai/api/share/{id}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"secret\": \"{secret}\"}"`
